NEW YORK, October 13, 2026 – The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc. (NYSE: GS) today reported net revenues of $18.68 billion
and net earnings of $5.29 billion for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026. Net revenues were $56.24 billion and net
earnings were $17.55 billion for the first nine months of 2026.
Diluted earnings per common share (EPS)1 was $17.01 for the third quarter of 2026 compared with $12.25 for the third quarter
of 2025 and $20.98 for the second quarter of 2026, and was $55.56 for the first nine months of 2026 compared with $37.33 for
the first nine months of 2025.
Annualized return on average common shareholders' equity (ROE)2 was 18.7% for the third quarter of 2026 and 20.7% for the
first nine months of 2026.
Book value per common share increased by 1.4% during the third quarter of 2026 and by 4.2% during the first nine months of
2026 to $372.64.
2
GOLDMAN SACHS REPORTS
THIRD QUARTER 2026 EARNINGS RESULTS
Net Revenues
Net revenues were $18.68 billion for the third quarter of 2026, 23% higher than
the third quarter of 2025 and 8% lower than the second quarter of 2026. The
increase compared with the third quarter of 2025 primarily reflected
significantly higher net revenues in Global Banking & Markets.
Net Revenues
$ in millions
3Q26
$18,679
Global Banking & Markets
Net revenues in Global Banking & Markets were $13.46 billion for the third
quarter of 2026, 32% higher than the third quarter of 2025 and 13% lower than
the second quarter of 2026.
Investment banking fees were $3.22 billion, 21% higher than the third quarter
of 2025, primarily due to higher net revenues in Advisory, reflecting an
increase in completed mergers and acquisitions volumes, and significantly
higher net revenues in Equity underwriting, primarily reflecting higher net
revenues from initial public offerings and secondary offerings. Net revenues in
Debt underwriting were also higher, primarily reflecting significantly higher net
revenues from investment-grade activity. The firm’s Investment banking fees
backlog3 decreased compared with the end of the second quarter of 2026 and
decreased slightly compared with the end of 2025.
Net revenues in Fixed Income, Currency and Commodities (FICC) were $3.47
billion, essentially unchanged compared with the third quarter of 2025. Net
revenues in FICC intermediation were lower, due to significantly lower net
revenues in mortgages and credit products and lower net revenues in interest
rate products, partially offset by significantly higher net revenues in currencies
and commodities. Net revenues in FICC financing were higher, primarily due to
higher net revenues in mortgages and structured lending.
Net revenues in Equities were $6.44 billion, 72% higher than the third quarter
of 2025, due to significantly higher net revenues in Equities financing (driven
by significantly higher net revenues in prime financing and portfolio financing)
and in Equities intermediation (primarily driven by significantly higher net
revenues in derivatives).
Net revenues in Other were $322 million, compared with $282 million for the
third quarter of 2025, primarily reflecting higher net revenues in transaction
banking.

Asset & Wealth Management
Net revenues in Asset & Wealth Management were $5.05 billion for the third
quarter of 2026, 14% higher than the third quarter of 2025 and 10% higher
than the second quarter of 2026. The increase compared with the third quarter
of 2025 reflected significantly higher Management and other fees and
Incentive fees, partially offset by significantly lower net revenues in
Investments and Private banking and lending.
The increase in Management and other fees primarily reflected the impact of
higher average assets under supervision. The increase in Incentive fees was
driven by fund distributions. The decrease in Investments net revenues
included net markdowns in debt investments compared with net markups in
the prior year period. The decrease in Private banking and lending net
revenues reflected the payment of interest on a previously impaired loan in the
prior year period.

Platform Solutions
Net revenues in Platform Solutions were $170 million for the third quarter of
2026, 72% lower than the third quarter of 2025 and 23% lower than the
second quarter of 2026. The decrease compared with the third quarter of 2025
primarily reflected net markdowns related to the Apple Card loan portfolio,
which was transferred to held for sale in the fourth quarter of 2025.

Provision for Credit Losses

Provision for credit losses was $368 million for the third quarter of 2026,
compared with $339 million for the third quarter of 2025 and $102 million for
the second quarter of 2026. Provisions for the third quarter of 2026 primarily
reflected impairments related to wholesale loans. Provisions for the third
quarter of 2025 primarily reflected net provisions related to the credit card
portfolio, which was transferred to held for sale in the fourth quarter of 2025.
4
GOLDMAN SACHS REPORTS
THIRD QUARTER 2026 EARNINGS RESULTS
Operating Expenses
Operating expenses were $11.31 billion for the third quarter of 2026, 20%
higher than the third quarter of 2025 and 3% lower than the second quarter of
2026. The firm's efficiency ratio3 was 59.4% for the first nine months of 2026,
compared with 62.1% for the first nine months of 2025.
The increase in operating expenses compared with the third quarter of 2025
primarily reflected significantly higher transaction based expenses and higher
compensation and benefits expenses (reflecting improved operating
performance). In addition, charitable contributions to Goldman Sachs Gives (in
other expenses) were significantly higher.
Net provisions for litigation and regulatory proceedings were $23 million for the
third quarter of 2026, compared with $131 million for the third quarter of 2025.
Headcount increased 3% compared with the end of the second quarter of
2026, reflecting the timing of campus hires.

The effective tax rate for the first nine months of 2026 was 20.4%, up from
18.5% for the first half of 2026, primarily due to a decrease in the impact of tax
benefits on the settlement of employee share-based awards.4
Other Matters
•On October 12, 2026, the Board of Directors of The Goldman Sachs
Group, Inc. declared a dividend of $5.00 per common share to be paid on
December 30, 2026 to common shareholders of record on December 2,
2026.
•During the quarter, the firm returned $4.49 billion of capital to common
shareholders, including $3.00 billion of common share repurchases (2.9
million shares at an average cost of $1,048.73) and $1.49 billion of
common stock dividends.3
•Global core liquid assets3 averaged $574 billion for the third quarter of
2026, compared with an average of $555 billion for the second quarter of
2026.

The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc. is a leading global financial institution that delivers a broad range of financial services to a
large and diversified client base that includes corporations, financial institutions, governments and individuals. Founded in
1869, the firm is headquartered in New York and maintains offices in all major financial centers around the world.
Cautionary Note Regarding Forward-Looking Statements
This press release contains “forward-looking statements” within the meaning of the safe harbor provisions of the U.S. Private
Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. Forward-looking statements are not historical facts or statements of current

possibly materially, from the anticipated results, financial condition and liquidity in these forward-looking statements. For
information about some of the risks and important factors that could affect the firm’s future results, financial condition and
liquidity, see “Risk Factors” in Part I, Item 1A of the firm’s Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2025.
Information regarding the firm’s assets under supervision, capital ratios, risk-weighted assets, supplementary leverage ratio,
balance sheet data, global core liquid assets and VaR consists of preliminary estimates. These estimates are forward-looking
statements and are subject to change, possibly materially, as the firm completes its financial statements.
Statements about the firm’s Investment banking fees backlog and future results also may constitute forward-looking
statements. Such statements are subject to the risk that transactions may be modified or may not be completed at all, and
related net revenues may not be realized or may be materially less than expected. Important factors that could have such a
result include, for underwriting transactions, a decline or weakness in general economic conditions, changes in international
trade policies, including the potential for new or increased tariffs, the continuation or worsening of the conflict in the Middle
East, volatility in the securities markets or an adverse development with respect to the issuer of the securities and, for financial
advisory transactions, a decline in the securities markets, an inability to obtain adequate financing, an adverse development
with respect to a party to the transaction or a failure to obtain a required regulatory approval. For information about other
important factors that could adversely affect the firm’s Investment banking fees, see “Risk Factors” in Part I, Item 1A of the
firm’s Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2025.
Conference Call
A conference call to discuss the firm’s financial results, outlook and related matters will be held at 9:30 am (ET). The call will
be open to the public. Members of the public who would like to listen to the conference call should dial 1-800-330-6730 (in the
U.S.) or 1-646-769-9500 (outside the U.S.) passcode number 7042022. The number should be dialed at least 10 minutes prior
to the start of the conference call. The conference call will also be accessible as an audio webcast through the Investor
Relations section of the firm’s website, www.goldmansachs.com/investor-relations. There is no charge to access the call. For
those unable to listen to the live broadcast, a replay will be available on the firm’s website beginning approximately three
hours after the event. Please direct any questions regarding obtaining access to the conference call to Goldman Sachs
Investor Relations, via e-mail, at gs-investor-relations@gs.com.
